 1 Cr

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Anil Ojha - Advocate for the appellant.

Shri Rahul Solanki -Ga appearing on behalf of Advocate
General.
I.A.No.11607/2025 is the 5th application under section 430(1) of the BNSS, 2023 for suspension of execution of sentence of appellant/accused.

Vide judgment dated 23.09.2022 in SC case No.295/2015 by 13th ASJ and Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012), Indore, appellant/accused has been convicted under sections 366, 376(2)(N) & 506 Part-II of the IPC and section 5(l), 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and has been sentenced for 7 years RI with fine of Rs.500/- u/s 366 IPC, 10 years RI with fine of Rs.2,000/- u/s 376(2)(N) of the IPC and 3 years RI u/s 506 Part-II of the IPC with further default stipulation.
The sentences of imprisonment have been ordered to run concurrently.

Appellant has been convicted and sentenced for committing penetrative sexual assault repeatedly with a child (PW/1), aged 16 years 3 months when he himself was of 36 years old as per arrest 2 CRA-8860-2022 memo Ex.P/9.

This repeat application has been preferred on the ground that he was granted liberty on 15.10.2024 to renew the prayer after six months and on 06.05.2025 after 3 months and he has undergone a sentence of about 3 years 6 months.
There is no DNA report and ossification test report discloses that she was 17 years 6 months old.
On the date of incident, he was only 30 years old.
There is evidence that he has been falsely implicated due to dispute with father of the victim.
He has no criminal antecedents and FSL report Ex.P/12 mentions that sperm and semen was not found on pubic hair (Ex.A/2) and vaginal slide (Ex.A/3).
The father of the victim has not mentioned the name of any person in the first information report.
There was no injury on the private part.

State has opposed the application submitting that all the grounds raised by the appellant/accused were consideredon 23.02.2023 when IA No.13357/2022 was rejected on merit and the age of the appellant was 36 years on the date of incident as per Ex.P/9.
The statement of child (PW/1) was very well supported by medical evidence.

The sperm was found on the underwear (Ex.A/1) of the victim and the report of medical officer Dr.Usha Choudhary (PW/3) also support the penetrative sexual assault and there is no requirement of presence of injury in the cases of penetrative sexual 3 CRA-8860-2022 assault especially towards children below the age of 18 years and there is no Vijay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185135074/

sentences.text: 1 rebuttal of the presumption under section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and the period of custody is not sufficient to enlarge the appellant on bail.

Considering the earlier rejection of the suspension on merit, the period of custody and the fact that the matter relates to sexual exploitation of a child victim by a matured person, this Court is not inclined to suspend the sentence passed against the appellant at present.
Accordingly, the application is rejected.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
